about

what is flobo?

flobo is a flowchart-first infinite canvas whiteboard. it's built for the people who think in diagrams — the ones who reach for a whiteboard before a document, who map processes before they write specs.

every node on the canvas is a real css element you fully control. border-radius, clip-path, per-side borders, opacity, fill colors — it's all yours. no locked-down shape libraries, no svg black boxes.

quickflow handles let you branch in any direction with a single click. drag from a handle onto an existing node to create a connection. double-click to edit. right-click for deep customization. it's designed to get out of your way.

flobo isn't trying to be everything. it's trying to be the best place to think visually about how things connect.

author's note

a few words

on the things i built and why i named them the way i did.

{/* ── flobo ── */}

flobo

{/* name meaning */}

name meaning

yes — flobo sounds like what a toddler who doesn't know how to speak yet would try to say when pronouncing the word "flowchart." flo from flow, bo from board.

but that's only partially true as a naming reason.

{/* why i named it flobo */}

why i named it flobo

the real reason is much dumber. i was tired of trying to remember which whiteboard app i used back in 2023. because they're all kind of named the same thing.

mindnode. graphxmind. xmind. mindxai.

i genuinely cannot tell you which one i liked. i've tried them all at various points. they blur together in my memory like a pile of apps that all have the word "mind" in them and use slightly different shades of blue for their icon.

so when it came time to name this thing, the only constraint was: i need to be able to remember this name six months from now without googling "flowchart whiteboard app that starts with m."

flobo. it's short. it's weird. it sounds like baby-talk. and that's exactly why i'll never forget it.

{/* why i built this */}

why i built this

coming soon.

{/* ── datawizardry ── */}

datawizardry

{/* the name */}

the name

this one's a bad pun born from phonetic drift. it's a tool for data visualization — data viz — datawiz — datawizard — datawizardry. that's it. that's the whole naming process.

{/* why i made this */}

why i made this

i made this to scratch my own itch.

i got fed up with charting platforms changing their pricing model every six months, or requiring login and card details just to make a chart, or limiting exports to watermarked static images on free tiers.

i don't need a feature-packed enterprise-grade business analytics tool. i just want polished, pixel-perfect charts for presenting social data. i didn't want to pay for something that should be simple.

so i knew i needed an alternative — one that doesn't lock you in, doesn't watermark your work, and doesn't make you sign up before you can even try it.

philosophy

less chrome, more canvas

most diagramming tools are designed around toolbars. flobo is designed around the canvas itself. the interface should disappear when you're working and appear only when you need it.

right-click is the primary interaction pattern. everything you need to customize a node or edge is one right-click away — no hunting through menus, panels, or property inspectors.

"the best tool is the one that doesn't make you think about the tool."

quickflow handles are the embodiment of this. you shouldn't have to switch to a "connector" tool, draw a line, then switch back. you should just click a direction and keep going.

shapes are real html elements with real css properties. not locked svgs, not canvas-rendered bitmaps. this means you get the full power of css — clip-path, border-radius, per-side borders, opacity, transforms — on every single node.

we believe diagramming should feel like sketching, not like programming. but when you want precision, it should be there.

purpose

why flobo exists

flobo exists because thinking visually shouldn't require a steep learning curve or a subscription to a bloated tool that does everything poorly.

it's for the quick diagram you need to sketch before a meeting. the process map you want to share with your team. the system architecture you're trying to reason through. the user flow you need to validate before you build.

flobo is opinionated about one thing: flowcharts should be the primary citizen. not an afterthought in a general-purpose whiteboard. not buried behind three menus in a documentation tool.

but flobo is also for the visual thinker — the person who retains information better when it's spatial, colorful, and hand-arranged. think visual sketchnotes. think bullet journal meets infinite canvas. the bujo planner aesthetic — intentional, personal, beautiful — applied to diagrams, notes, and knowledge maps for better presentation and retention of information.

it's where structured diagramming meets freeform visual journaling. the same canvas that holds your system architecture can hold your sketchnoted meeting notes, your hand-styled reading list, your color-coded project tracker — all with the same pixel-level control.

the purpose is simple — make the gap between "i have an idea about how these things connect" and "here's a diagram that shows it" as small as humanly possible.

no accounts. no paywalls. no onboarding wizards. open the canvas and start.

wobbles & scribbles

wobble-scribble

organic, hand-drawn visual elements for canvases that feel alive — not clinical.

{/* wobbles */}

wobbles

wobbles are general-purpose recolorable shape blobs — organic, irregular, soft-edged forms procedurally generated on the canvas. think of them as the anti-rectangle: no sharp corners, no grid alignment, no geometric rigidity.

use them as background containers, section dividers, decorative accents, or highlight regions. each wobble is unique — generated from randomised bezier curves with controllable amplitude, frequency, and smoothness.

scribbles

scribbles are hand-doodled drawings — small illustrative sketches that add warmth, character, and visual context to your canvases. arrows with personality, underlines with flair, stars, check marks, boxes, banners, and decorative flourishes.

they're the visual vocabulary of sketchnoting and bullet journaling, brought to the infinite canvas. use them to annotate, emphasise, decorate, or just make your diagram feel less like a corporate slide deck.

scribbles will ship as a curated library of recolorable, resizable svg elements — plus a draw-your-own mode where your freehand strokes become reusable scribble assets.

together

wobbles and scribbles are the layer between "clinical diagram" and "hand-drawn sketch." use wobbles as soft containers and scribbles as expressive annotations — together they turn any canvas into something that feels intentional, personal, and alive.

datawizardry

datawizardry / maps

interactive maps

interactive world maps for data storytelling — filter, theme, and explore geographic data right on the canvas.

world maps

drop an interactive world map onto the canvas like any other node. zoom into continents, countries, or regions. hover for tooltips, click for detail panels. think tasmap.app and wandery — but embedded in your diagram, bound to your data.

data filtering

bind datasets to map regions. filter by any dimension — time, category, value range — and watch the map update in real time. choropleth shading, bubble overlays, and pin markers will all respond to the same filter controls.

filters can be driven by other nodes on the canvas — select a category in a table node and the map recolours to match. everything is connected.

map themes

switch between visual themes — light, dark, satellite, minimal, vintage, illustrated, and more. map themes are independent of your canvas theme, so a dark-mode dashboard can hold a light vintage map if that's what the data calls for.

custom color palettes for choropleth shading, adjustable stroke widths for borders, and label density controls so you show exactly the level of geographic detail you need.

projections & views

choose between mercator, robinson, orthographic (globe), and other projections. lock to a specific region or let users pan and zoom freely. the map is as flexible as any other canvas element.

exportable

like everything in flobo, map visualizations export as interactive html/js bundles — not static screenshots. embed them in presentations, blog posts, or host them standalone. the interactivity travels with the export.

const THEME_IDS = Object.keys(THEMES);

function hexToRgb(hex: string): string {
  const result = /^#?([a-f\d]{2})([a-f\d]{2})([a-f\d]{2})$/i.exec(hex);
  return result
    ? `${parseInt(result[1], 16)} ${parseInt(result[2], 16)} ${parseInt(
        result[3],
        16,
      )}`
    : '0 0 0';
}

function applyTheme(themeId: string) {
  const theme = THEMES[themeId];
  if (!theme) return;

  const root = document.documentElement;
  const { colors, fonts, radius, shadow } = theme;

  root.style.setProperty('--background', colors.background);

  root.style.setProperty('--secondary', colors.secondary);
  root.style.setProperty('--secondary-foreground', colors.secondaryForeground);
  root.style.setProperty('--muted', colors.muted);

    '--destructive-foreground',
    colors.destructiveForeground,

  root.style.setProperty('--border', colors.border);
  root.style.setProperty('--input', colors.input);
  root.style.setProperty('--ring', colors.ring);
  root.style.setProperty('--chart-1', colors.chart1);
  root.style.setProperty('--chart-2', colors.chart2);
  root.style.setProperty('--chart-3', colors.chart3);
  root.style.setProperty('--chart-4', colors.chart4);

/**
 * This component is not meant to be consumed by Zite generated code, but just there
 * to help developing components and testing them with the different Zite themes.
 * @internal
 */
export function ThemeSwitcher() {
  const [activeTheme, setActiveTheme] = useState('default');
  const [radius, setRadius] = useState(0.5);

  function handleSelect(id: string) {
    setActiveTheme(id);
    applyTheme(id);
    setRadius(parseFloat(THEMES[id].radius));
  }

  function handleRadiusChange([value]: number[]) {
    setRadius(value);
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--radius', `${value}rem`);
  }

  return (
    <Collapsible className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
        <Select value={activeTheme} onValueChange={handleSelect}>
          <SelectTrigger className="w-48">
            <SelectValue />
          </SelectTrigger>
          <SelectContent>
            {THEME_IDS.map(id => {
              const theme = THEMES[id];
              return (
                <SelectItem key={id} value={id}>
                  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
                    <div className="flex h-3.5 w-8 overflow-hidden rounded-sm shrink-0">
                      {theme.previewPalette.map((color, i) => (
                        <div
                          key={i}
                          className="flex-1"
                          style={{ backgroundColor: color }}
                        />
                      ))}
                    </div>
                    {theme.name}
                  </div>
                </SelectItem>
              );
            })}
          </SelectContent>
        </Select>

        <div className="flex items-center gap-3 w-48">
          <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground shrink-0">Radius</span>
          <Slider
            min={0}
            max={3}
            step={0.05}
            value={[radius]}
            onValueChange={handleRadiusChange}
          />
          <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground w-10 shrink-0">
            {radius.toFixed(2)}
          </span>
        </div>

        <CollapsibleTrigger className="flex items-center gap-1 text-sm text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground [&[data-state=open]>svg]:rotate-180">
          <ChevronDown className="size-4 transition-transform duration-200" />
          Colors
        </CollapsibleTrigger>
      </div>

      <CollapsibleContent>
        <div className="columns-[200px] space-y-1">
          {COLOR_VARS.map(variable => (
            <div
              key={variable}
              className="flex items-center gap-2 py-0.5 break-inside-avoid"
            >
              <div
                className="size-6 shrink-0 rounded-sm border border-border"
                style={{ backgroundColor: `hsl(var(${variable}))` }}
              />
              <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground font-mono truncate">
                {variable}
              </span>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      </CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  );
}
